lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Education appears before the more relevant finance experience.
items.because: That ordering delays the experience most likely to support the candidate’s current direction.

items.says: The older Student Investment Fund entry does not add a clear next step after several years of finance work.
items.because: Its full detail may take attention from more recent experience.

items.says: The ongoing caddie work is written in past tense.
The service tasks do not state their effect on members.
The caddie duties do not connect the current role to the résumé’s finance direction.
The tournament bullet does not say what you did, and “Helped” is vague.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what contribution you made to the event.

items.says: “Helped” is past tense for a current role.
items.because: It conflicts with the role dates and makes the work sound like it may have ended.

items.says: The tournament bullet gives neither the event’s scale nor what your contribution accomplished.
“Close efficiency by 40%” does not identify the measure or comparison behind the improvement.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what changed or the practical size of the improvement.

items.says: The standardized capital-plan rules are described without saying what they changed.
The explanation of the capital-plan rules is wordy.
The board-pack commentary is not tied to a decision or follow-up action.
“Explaining each line more than 5% off budget” is awkward and makes the threshold hard to scan.
FCFE is discounted at the wrong rate: cost of equity, not WACC, is normally used.
items.because: Discounting cash available to equity holders at WACC mismatches the cash flow and discount rate.

items.says: The acquisition valuation gives the method but not what it supported or concluded.
The group EBITDA margin is calculated incorrectly by adding the units’ margins.
items.because: A group margin is total EBITDA divided by total revenue, not the sum of unit margins.

items.says: The group-margin bullet does not explain what the reporting or calculation contributed.
The 45% group margin has no reporting period or comparison.
The USD 40M debt-repayment outcome is buried after the forecast details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the notable result at the end of a long bullet.

items.says: The underwriting bullet does not identify the analysis used to assess borrower creditworthiness.
items.because: The count and outcome do not show the analytical skill behind the decisions.

items.says: The loan outcome is a long add-on after the underwriting details.
The approval result is buried after the review description.
items.because: Starting with the process delays the most compelling result for a scanning reader.

items.says: “Reviewed 3 years of declined applications” is ambiguous about when the applications were declined or reviewed.
“My findings” uses a first-person pronoun in a résumé bullet.
“Writes” incorrectly uses present tense for a role that ended in December 2022.
items.because: It places the checklist work outside the role’s dates and can make the responsibility seem current.

items.says: The 6% comparison comes after the valuation methods.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the result.

items.says: “A 1-point change” does not state the direction or starting and ending discount rates.
“It” could refer to either the model or the note.
The FP&A support bullet does not identify a specific contribution or deliverable.
The FP&A support bullet gives no outcome from the work.
The committee’s repeated use of the report comes after the report description.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the clearest evidence of the report’s value.

items.says: The USD 600M cash forecast and its results duplicate the later Stonebridge achievement.
items.because: The same achievement appears attributed to roles several years apart, leaving its ownership inconsistent.

items.says: “Error” does not say what was measured, and “about 4%” lacks a stated error basis.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the 4% represents or what the forecast was compared against.

items.says: The cash-forecast bullet does not say how the forecast was developed.
items.because: A reader cannot assess the forecasting approach.

items.says: The Student Investment Fund bullets shift among unrelated types of work without reading as one student-fund contribution.
